note: For a tail call from a vararg function, the frame-correction delta is computed from the call info, not from the arguments actually on the stack.
When B is zero (vararg call), the argument count is derived from L->top; this count is later used to move the whole call frame down.
The tail-call path reuses the current CallInfo and rewinds func before handing the frame to luaD_pretailcall.

code: for (i = 0; i < narg1; i++)  /* move down function and arguments */
note: luaD_pretailcall moves function plus arguments down into the reused frame, duplicating (and diverging from) the frame setup that luaD_precall performs for regular calls.
The stack check happens after the move and without the pointer-preserving variant used by luaD_precall, leaving the tail-call frame setup inconsistent with regular calls.
Frame and top are recomputed from the moved-down function position, completing the divergent tail-call frame construction.
Execution continues with the reused CallInfo, so the tail-called function runs with a frame built by luaD_pretailcall instead of luaD_precall.
